issues.legal_issue: Evidence given by an unavailable witness in an earlier stage of the same judicial proceeding is admissible at a later stage when the opposing party had both the right and the opportunity to cross-examine the witness.
material_facts: The witness had testified before the committing Magistrate, but could not be traced for the Sessions trial despite searches in the relevant localities and further inquiries in Nepal.

The accused was represented by counsel when the witness testified before the committing Magistrate and had the right to cross-examine him, but counsel declined to do so and reserved cross-examination for the Sessions Court.
issues.conclusion: The witness's evidence before the committing Magistrate was admissible at the Sessions trial.
issues.legal_principle: Section 33 of the Evidence Act permits evidence given by a witness in a judicial proceeding to be used at a later stage of the same proceeding when the witness cannot be found, provided the adverse party had both the right and the opportunity to cross-examine. Sections 207 and 207A(4) and (5) of the Criminal Procedure Code gave the accused the right to cross-examine prosecution witnesses before the committing Magistrate; choosing to reserve cross-examination did not remove that opportunity. Dal Bahadur Singh v. Bijai Bahadur Singh was relied on for the requirement of both right and opportunity. State of Assam v. Ramani Mohan Chanda was distinguished because the accused there had not been given an opportunity to cross-examine.

rule.if: criminal_trial and later_stage_same_judicial_proceeding and prior_testimony_given_in_judicial_proceeding and witness_untraceable_after_reasonable_search and adverse_party_had_cross_examination_right and adverse_party_had_cross_examination_opportunity

predicates.criminal_trial: The evidence was tendered in a criminal trial.
predicates.later_stage_same_judicial_proceeding: The earlier testimony was offered at a later stage of the same judicial proceeding.
predicates.prior_testimony_given_in_judicial_procee: The witness had given the testimony in an earlier judicial proceeding.
predicates.witness_untraceable_after_reasonable_sea: Those seeking the witness made reasonable efforts to find the witness but could not do so.
predicates.adverse_party_had_cross_examination_righ: The opposing party had the right to cross-examine the witness when the earlier testimony was given.
predicates.adverse_party_had_cross_examination_oppo: The opposing party had an opportunity to cross-examine the witness but chose not to use it then.

issues.definition: If testimony was given in a judicial proceeding and is offered at a later stage of that same proceeding, and the witness cannot be found after reasonable searches while the opposing party had the right and opportunity to cross-examine, the testimony is admissible.

issues.legal_issue: Circumstantial evidence, including reliable and corroborated evidence placing the accused at the scene and evidence of motive and subsequent conduct, can support affirmance of a murder conviction.
material_facts: The prosecution evidence showed longstanding and serious disputes between the accused and the deceased over their father's property.
A witness testified that he saw the accused enter the house at about midnight and later heard groaning; a report recording the witness's account was made before the murder was discovered.
The deceased was alone in the house before the incident, and the evidence placed only the accused and the deceased inside it at the relevant time.
The accused left the area after the incident and, despite learning that something serious had happened to his brother, made no inquiry to establish what had occurred.
The trial court convicted the accused of murder and imposed a death sentence, and the High Court upheld the conviction and sentence.
issues.conclusion: The circumstantial evidence established the accused's guilt; the appeal was dismissed and the conviction and death sentence were confirmed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on the cumulative force of the circumstances proved in the case, particularly the witness's evidence of the accused's presence at the house, corroboration by the report made before discovery of the murder, the fact that no one else was in the house, the property dispute, and the accused's conduct after the event. It found no reason to differ from the trial court and High Court on the witness's evidence. No earlier case was cited for this merits determination.

rule.if: appeal_from_murder_conviction and strong_motive_for_the_killing and reliable_witness_places_accused_at_scene and contemporaneous_report_corrobates_witness and accused_and_victim_were_only_people_in_house and accused_avoided_inquiry_despite_knowledge

predicates.appeal_from_murder_conviction: The case is an appeal challenging a conviction for murder.
predicates.strong_motive_for_the_killing: The evidence showed a serious dispute providing a strong motive for the killing.
predicates.reliable_witness_places_accused_at_scene: A witness whose evidence the court accepted placed the accused at the scene at the relevant time.
predicates.contemporaneous_report_corrobates_witnes: A report made before discovery of the crime recorded the witness's account of the accused's presence and related events.
predicates.accused_and_victim_were_only_people_in_h: The evidence showed that only the accused and the victim were in the house at the relevant time.
predicates.accused_avoided_inquiry_despite_knowledg: The accused knew that something serious had happened to the victim but did not make inquiries to find out what had occurred.

issues.definition: When an appeal against a murder conviction presents a strong motive, reliable evidence placing the accused at the scene corroborated by a contemporaneous report, proof that only the accused and victim were in the house, and avoidance of inquiry despite knowledge, the conviction and sentence are upheld.
